speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Dick, thou wilt hear it from me or from the next bench, and I had rather it were from me. A Cambridge man has put two words by my name.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Two words. For the king, or for the poems thou art always being told are the better half of thee?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Field says for the poems. Not for a king in Shoreditch, and not for a boy under a wall.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Then Field may keep the poems. I will keep the king.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You have heard more than I meant for the next bench, Will.

speaker: will_kemp
text: I heard sweet. A man may hear sweet from the next bench and not be a thief. I will sit with it.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Sit with it, then. Do not spend it all tonight. He has a tooth, and you have a spoon.

speaker: will_kemp
text: You may have the spoon's work. I am not eating. I am only trying the fit of it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Eat your supper, Will. The margin will keep till you are hungry again.

speaker: will_kemp
text: It will keep. You will tell me if it pinches.
